title: Weekly Update - Plans For 2030, Huge Patch, Corruption Fix, PC Mods & More! - RuneScape Dragonwilds
author: IAmWaved
chapters: Plans For 2030, 1 Saga Each Year (Recent Interview)
description:

transcript.text: Hello folks, we do have an absolute ton to get through today as not only have we just had our first substantial update
since the 1.0 and console release fixing some big save corruption issues and adding some additional content, quality
of life, and bug fixes, but we also have a recent interview with Jagex that confirms the game should receive
continuous updates right up to and possibly beyond the year 2030. In addition to this, we have a recent model
two available right now that helps showcase exactly what we can expect from the full mod support coming next year.
We'll be recapping the rest of the 2026 and 2027 roadmaps as well as of course touching on the game's most recent
issues and maybe even a few of the topics here and there, too. Plenty for us to get through and as always, we are
not wasting any time, so let's get started. Okay, so the first topic I want to briefly cover for today would be the
recent save corruption issues. There were three in total that have occurred since the 1.0 console launch and
seemingly now it has been a few days since they've all finally been resolved, it would appear that they are definitely
now fixed. As I haven't really seen any mention of players still having problems
and the devs haven't made any additional announcements, either. There could of course be future issues regarding save
corruption as the game is updated multiple times per month and with every new update, something else might get
temporarily broken. But as of right now, they've finally all been resolved and so theoretically, no one should be having
these particular issues anymore. As somewhat of an extension to this topic, the recent 1.0.1 update we received just
a few days ago has brought along some new issues with it. Not quite as game-breaking as the issues we just
covered, but nonetheless, they are causing problems here and there. We did actually receive word on this just a few
days ago, but because of today's hotfix addressing all of this anyway, we can skip that original announcement and just
read out today's notes. And so, they do go as follows. Hello adventurers, we're deploying a hotfix to resolve a few
outstanding issues. Dedicated servers will need to be restarted to apply this fix. Resolved an issue where the
corrupted save file detected model pop-up was unfocused, meaning controller users weren't able to bypass it. Fixed
an issue where dedicated servers would encounter a crash when ranged special attacks hit certain enemies. Switch two
players, an important note for you, this update will not be hitting your consoles today. However, the team has found a
solution in which you will be able to still cross play with others who have already updated. This comes from your
feedback about not wanting to be blocked from cross play whilst Nintendo approves updates. We're aware of the issues
affecting the air staffs fourth combo hit currently not applying on hit damage and a freeze when splitting stacks
within chests. These are issues that we're on track to fix, but we want to give these adequate time to test and
verify these fixes prior to submission. We're targeting a fix for these next week with the requisite time taken for
it to be processed by console partner platforms. Now, firstly, I do just have to say I absolutely love how fast and
transparent the devs are at every single turn here. Be it as it may, that save corruption and the range of issues the
game has suffered from for a little while now isn't necessarily great for any game. The sheer level of
responsiveness, taking ownership, and clearly communicating with us players is practically unheard of within today's
gaming climate. And so, party hats off to the devs because whilst I've only been following them for a few months
now, they have not relented on this work ethic or level of responsiveness, which in my own opinion goes a very long way
in taking some of the sting out of these particular issues. Fortunately, the current list of problems isn't all that
egregious right now anyway. They say a fix should be going live next week and so naturally I'll report on it again
then. But, that does just about cover all of the current and past problems that are being / have been addressed.
Now, as for the 1.0.1 update itself, we have had a range of upgrades included being separate slots for both rings and
amulets instead of a shared accessory slot, increased inventory space, a new and better compost bucket, new special
attacks for all three ranged weapon types, which now that I've played I can confirm are a very nice addition. And
then, we do also have a new jumping attack and whilst this could be better realized, it's still absolutely a step
in the right direction nonetheless. Outside of these new additions, there was naturally an absolute ton of quality
of life tweaks and bug fixes, too. If you'd like a full rundown, then feel free to check out this video here.
Otherwise, it's far too much to nutshell or recap. What we can expect moving forward though is another update around
this time in November. That should be a very similar size, too. Also including some new upgrades and additions. As of
right now, we don't truly know what they may be as some of the things included just a few days ago were quite a
surprise. But of course, just those updates arrive, I'll also be covering them all in full. That then does take us
right up to the Lumin update in December, which has been showcased quite a bit already. We know elves, a new
area, the prayer skill, new equipment items, a building kit, songs, fairy rings, puzzles, and so much more is on
the way. But I'm sure outside of this, there's still a ton we don't currently know about. If you'd like a video
dedicated to exactly that, then feel free to check out this one right here. Otherwise, I'm sure I will be covering
it all again between now and when it actually arrives. This does of course then take us through to 2027, in which
we have had quite a bit showcased already. We know the hunting skill and various other things arrive within the
first three months. And then we know the slayer skill and vampires arrive in the final three months. However, we have no
idea what the two confirmed skills for mid-year might be. And then outside of this, there will be a ton of content in
all of these updates that we just don't know about until it all arrives. But I'm sure some of it will eventually be
showcased as and when we get closer to the actual updates themselves. Another thing we know is arriving next year is
full mod support for all platforms through CurseForge. To create mods, players will need access to a PC.
However, to browse and install them, you can use a console. And so at the very least, all players will have full access
to browse and install. Whilst this is still quite a while away, just this week I've seen a recent fan-made mod floating
around online in which all four dragon types are available to ride around on in game. And I have to say it does get me
really excited for what is to come. This current mod, I believe, is available over on Nexus Mods right now, and so
I'll have that link below for anyone interested. Otherwise, I just wanted to showcase to everyone just how much
potential full mod support actually brings. Now, what that does basically cover everything we know right up until
the end of 2027. And whilst the devs at RuneFest touched on Dragon Wilds having a long and fruitful future in an actual
interview at the RuneFest event itself, they shared more details than before. And so, whilst I've cherry-picked this
for all of the good bits, the article does go as follows. RuneScape Dragon Wilds devs confirm a string of sagas are
in the work as player support is higher than expected. In a discussion at RuneFest, executive producer Jesse
America and creative director Rick Cherek confirmed that there are already plans for multiple sagas that will
result in years of support for RuneScape Dragon Wilds. There is a string of sagas planned, the developers told us in an
interview at the event, and we're committed to the game for the long haul. With each saga currently taking up a
year of content each, we should see support for the game stretching into 2030. Jagex confirmed that the crafting
game has been a massive success for the studio with the game boasting millions of players. In the interview, it was
confirmed that close to 3 million people have played the game now, confirming that those numbers are all unique
players. For its 1.0 release, RuneScape Dragon Wilds also launched in Xbox Game Pass and on the higher tiers of
PlayStation Plus. Jagex told the outlet that the game's reception via those services is not only high, but higher
than usual. Sony and Microsoft are extremely happy with results and interaction with RuneScape Dragon Wilds,
they said, higher than what they normally say. Of course, despite the fact that this is Jagex's first console
game ever, the game has been extremely well received on all platforms, although its Nintendo Switch 2 port does exhibit
some issues. Now, of course, whilst quite brief, what we can take from this is that Dragon Wilds has proven itself
to be a game worth investing in for Jagex. They have a track record for trying new games and then eventually
scrapping them because they never actually take off. And so, it is very nice to see a new and third pillar to
the franchise, that doesn't just replicate the same MMO RPG elements that made RuneScape what it is in the first
place. The Blood Crystal Saga will take up the entirety of 2027 and consist of 12 major updates, four of which will be
massive and include tons of new content, and then we can pretty much expect that that exact same pattern of updates for
each and every new saga that takes place there afterwards. It's honestly going to be pretty crazy to see just how
different the game looks in even half a year's time, let alone two or three years, but just like the rest of you,
I'm hooked and very excited for what's to come. Now, that was quite a lot to get through, folks, but I hope I've done
